summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API using multipartbody.NewFile and verifies multipart encoding plus retry behavior. B changes the required signature, adds explicitly forbidden association APIs, and introduces broader, unsafe buffering behavior.
reasons: A exposes the required signature with opts ...FilesOption; B instead introduces AddFileOption, breaking the exact API contract and changing established FilesOption behavior.
B adds deal/person/organization/product/activity/project/lead association fields despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields.
A reuses multipartbody.NewFile directly. B unnecessarily expands the helper with NewFileWithFields solely to support forbidden functionality.

B's makeBodyReplayable globally buffers every non-replayable RawClient body, an out-of-scope retry refactor. Worse, it silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after partially consuming the source, potentially sending a truncated remainder instead of propagating the reader failure required by the contract and expected from Raw.Do semantics generally viable. A's seekable-body change is also out of scope, but is narrower and does not swallow read errors in this way. (Correction: expected from Raw.Do semantics generally.) A's implementation still propagates multipart source-reader failures via NewFile. (Malformed prose aside, the core issue remains B swallowing raw-body read errors.) remain). A is preferable overall; its API fidelity dominates despite notable contract deviations. Typed concise assessment: A exact API; B not mergeable under frozen contract.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option/request/response logic instead of routing the encoded body through Add, violating the single-path requirement.
It changes RawClient and Files.Add retry/ownership semantics for seekable readers, despite the instruction not to refactor retry machinery or change Add behavior.
The added tests do not explicitly cover source-reader errors.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong public signature and does not preserve FilesOption behavior.
It adds explicitly forbidden association options and duplicate option machinery.

Upload bypasses FilesService.Add rather than routing through it as required validly directly via Raw.Do). (The bypass is visible in the diff.) remain). It calls Raw.Do directly and duplicates response handling. (Clear contract violation.) final note). Additionally, Upload retry itself is not tested with streamed content; the retry test exercises Add instead. source-reader failures are also untested. makeBodyReplayable silently returns after io.ReadAll failure with a partially consumed request body, risking corrupted requests and suppressing the source error. This broad global buffering also changes memory and streaming behavior for unrelated RawClient calls.
